long_biography.plain_text:
Before an owner was secured, Mehmet Karabeyoglu committed to building a fifty-metre yacht that would carry the Turquoise name. The speculative project expressed the operating style he brought from mechanical-engineering studies in England: take technical control, build substantial capability and compete internationally. He had entered yacht construction in 1990, and the success of that first large vessel helped turn his young company into a credible shipyard platform for complex commissioned projects.

The combination of Turquoise with Proteksan created a builder focused on large custom yachts for overseas clients. As founder and chief executive, Karabeyoglu championed in-house production of hulls, superstructures, engineering systems and finishes, then guided facility expansion under new majority ownership. This approach kept technical knowledge, craftsmanship and production decisions within the yard while it pursued larger commissions. After decades shaping the company and its international reputation, he and fellow founder Necdet Salgur stepped away from management in 2023, leaving the established business to its next leadership team.
